title: Uniform parameter Taylor coefficients on a compact set
statement:
Work over $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $d\geq0$, let $U\subset\mathbf C$ and $P\subset\mathbf C^d$ be open, and let $K\subset U$ be compact. Let $g:U\times P\to\mathbf C$ be holomorphic, meaning locally represented by a convergent complex power series in all coordinates. Fix $w_0\in P$ and $s>0$ such that $Q_s=\{w:|w_j-w_{0j}|\leq s\ (1\leq j\leq d)\}\subset P$. There are a finite real number $M\geq0$ and continuous functions $a_\alpha:K\to\mathbf C$, for $\alpha\in\mathbf N^d$, such that
$$|a_\alpha(\zeta)|\leq M s^{-|\alpha|},\qquad g(\zeta,w_0+v)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^d}a_\alpha(\zeta)v^\alpha\quad(\zeta\in K,\ |v_j|<s).$$
Here $|\alpha|=\sum_j\alpha_j$ and $v^\alpha=\prod_jv_j^{\alpha_j}$. For every $0<\rho<s$, this series converges absolutely and uniformly for $\zeta\in K$ and $|v_j|\leq\rho$: explicitly, the sum of the supremum norms of its terms is finite and at most $M(1-\rho/s)^{-d}$. One may take $M=\max_{K\times Q_s}|g|$ when $K$ is nonempty. For $d=0$ there is one multi-index, of degree zero, and the assertion reads $a_0(\zeta)=g(\zeta,w_0)$.

source.place: I §3.A (3.3), I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9): compact-uniform parameter Taylor expansion and iterated Cauchy bounds; worker-formulated auxiliary, PDF WANTED locally, not read in this repair.

proof.text: If $K=\varnothing$, take $M=0$ and the empty functions $a_\alpha$; all supremum norms on the empty set are zero. Henceforth suppose $K\ne\varnothing$. Holomorphic $g$ is continuous by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. By [lem-sfb-complex-polydisc-compactness], $K\times Q_s$ is compact and nonempty (it contains $(\zeta,w_0)$ for $\zeta\in K$). Apply [lem-sfb-compact-real-function-minimum] to the continuous real function $-|g|$ on this compact set. Thus $M=\max_{K\times Q_s}|g|$ exists, is finite and nonnegative, and bounds $|g|$ there. If $d=0$, take $a_0(\zeta)=g(\zeta,w_0)$; continuity, the bound, and the single-term series assertion follow immediately. We now assume $d>0$.

source.place: Preliminaries for the compact-uniform Cauchy estimate (I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9)). Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.

proof.text:
Put $\theta_j(t)=w_{0j}+s e^{it}$ and define, with the indicated order of nested ordinary integrals,
$$a_\alpha(\zeta)=(2\pi)^{-d}s^{-|\alpha|}\int_0^{2\pi}\cdots\int_0^{2\pi}g(\zeta,\theta_1(t_1),\ldots,\theta_d(t_d))e^{-i\sum_j\alpha_jt_j}\,dt_d\cdots dt_1.$$
All these integrals exist. Here are also the continuity and bound checks, rather than an appeal to parameter integration: $g$ is uniformly continuous on $K\times Q_s$ by [lem-sfb-compact-uniform-continuity]. After integrating any fixed set of the last coordinates, the difference between two values at the remaining arguments is bounded by $(2\pi)^k$ times the supremum of the original difference, times the fixed scalar $s^{-|\alpha|}$. This follows by applying the integral bound of [lem-sfb-normal-series-interval-integration] $k$ times. The exponential factors have modulus one and are continuous; factors in unintegrated coordinates may be pulled outside. Uniform continuity therefore makes each intermediate integral continuous in its remaining arguments. Induction starts with continuous $g$, so each next one-variable integrand is continuous and its ordinary integral exists. At $k=d$ this proves continuity of $a_\alpha$ on $K$. Applying the same bound to $|g|\leq M$ gives $|a_\alpha(\zeta)|\leq (2\pi)^{-d}s^{-|\alpha|}(2\pi)^dM=Ms^{-|\alpha|}$.

source.place: Construction of the Cauchy coefficients and their continuity and estimates (I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9)). Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.

proof.text:
Fix $\zeta\in K$ and $v$ with $|v_j|<s$. Every coordinate slice of $w\mapsto g(\zeta,w)$ is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of its closed disc: fixing the other coordinates is composition with an affine analytic map by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations], and $Q_s\subset P$ with $P$ open supplies that neighbourhood. Thus the slice is continuous on the closed disc and complex differentiable in its interior by [lem-sfb-analytic-germ-differentiable]. Repeatedly apply [lem-sfb-cauchy-circle-formula] in the coordinates, always to a slice of $g$ with the other coordinates fixed, not to an integral whose holomorphy is unproved. For $k=0$ the expression is $g(\zeta,w_0+v)$; replacing, inside the innermost integrand, the value of $g$ as a function of coordinate $k+1$ (the coordinates $1,\ldots,k$ already on their circles, the coordinates after $k+1$ still at $w_{0j}+v_j$) by its Cauchy integral gives the expression with $k+1$ nested circle integrals, the new integral in $t_{k+1}$ being the innermost; the kernel factors of $t_1,\ldots,t_k$ do not depend on $t_{k+1}$ and move inside by linearity. Thus $t_1$ is the outermost and $t_d$ the innermost variable, the order fixed in step 2. The substitution $z_j=w_{0j}+se^{it_j}$ has $dz_j=ise^{it_j}dt_j$, so each normalized Cauchy factor becomes $(2\pi)^{-1}(1-v_j/(se^{it_j}))^{-1}dt_j$. Consequently
$$g(\zeta,w_0+v)=(2\pi)^{-d}\int_0^{2\pi}\cdots\int_0^{2\pi}g(\zeta,\theta(t))\prod_{j=1}^d(1-v_j/(se^{it_j}))^{-1}\,dt_d\cdots dt_1.$$
All denominators are nonzero and bounded away from zero by $1-|v_j|/s$. The continuity argument of step 2 applies also to these continuous kernel factors, so the nested integrals exist. No exchange of integration order is used.

source.place: Iterated one-variable Cauchy formula (I §3.A (3.3)). Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.

proof.text:
Choose $0<\rho<s$ and put $r=\rho/s<1$. For $|v_j|\leq\rho$, [lem-sfb-scalar-geometric-series] gives
$$(1-v_j/(se^{it_j}))^{-1}=\sum_{n\geq0}(v_j/s)^n e^{-int_j}.$$
Apply [lem-sfb-absolute-series-product] repeatedly, starting with the empty product $1$ and adjoining one coordinate at a time. It gives the absolutely convergent multi-index expansion of the product of kernels, and likewise
$$\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^d}r^{|\alpha|}=\prod_{j=1}^d\sum_{n\geq0}r^n=(1-r)^{-d}.$$
The integrand term belonging to $\alpha$ is $g(\zeta,\theta(t))s^{-|\alpha|}v^\alpha e^{-i\sum_j\alpha_jt_j}$. Its modulus is at most $M r^{|\alpha|}$ simultaneously for $\zeta\in K$, every real angle tuple $t$, and $|v_j|\leq\rho$. The scalar multiple by $M$ preserves summability, so these are summable bounds. [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] also gives absolute convergence of the integrand series.

source.place: Geometric expansion of the Cauchy kernels (I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9)). Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.

proof.text:
Integrate the series in step 4 first in $t_d$, then in $t_{d-1}$, and so forth. At the first integration, the index set $\mathbf N^d$ is countable and every term is a continuous function of the integration variable on all $\mathbf R$. Its supremum norm on $[0,2\pi]$ is at most $Mr^{|\alpha|}$; the sum of these norms is finite by [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination]. Thus [lem-sfb-normal-series-interval-integration] allows the first interchange. Inductively, after $k$ integrations every term is continuous in the remaining variables by the argument of step 2, and has modulus at most $(2\pi)^kMr^{|\alpha|}$, by the integral bound in that same cited node. The majorant remains summable, so its termwise-integration clause applies again. This establishes all $d$ interchanges with no Fubini assumption. For each $\alpha$, the constant $v^\alpha$ pulls outside the integrals; the remaining normalized integral is exactly $a_\alpha(\zeta)$ from step 2. Combining with step 3 proves
$$g(\zeta,w_0+v)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^d}a_\alpha(\zeta)v^\alpha\qquad(|v_j|\leq\rho).$$

source.place: Termwise integration of the normally convergent kernel series, using the preceding Cauchy expansion. Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.

proof.text:
For the same $\rho$, let $N_\alpha$ be the supremum of $|a_\alpha(\zeta)v^\alpha|$ over $\zeta\in K$ and $|v_j|\leq\rho$. Step 2 gives $N_\alpha\leq Mr^{|\alpha|}$. The majorant computed in step 4 and [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] show
$$\sum_\alpha N_\alpha\leq M(1-\rho/s)^{-d}<\infty.$$
For any finite set $F$ of multi-indices the absolute value of the remaining sum is at most $\sum_{\alpha\notin F}N_\alpha$, again by domination. Summability makes this tail smaller than any prescribed positive tolerance for all sufficiently large finite $F$, independently of $\zeta,v$. This is absolute and uniform convergence, understood as the net of finite subsums. Finally any $v$ with all $|v_j|<s$ admits $\rho$ with $\max_j|v_j|<\rho<s$, so step 5 supplies the asserted equality on the whole open polydisc. The cases $K=\varnothing$ and $d=0$ were already settled in step 1.

source.place: Uniform tails and the stated sum of supremum norms; elementary consequences of the common Cauchy bound. Agent argument; Demailly PDF unavailable locally.
